Why is it that economic coercion is the only solution when dealing with a country that is struggling with bankruptcy. The IMF's austerity measures forced upon the country in need in order to secure the necessary funds to stay afloat breed a dependency that is very rarely ever relinquished after the fact. These draconian austerity measures have been seen to do much more harm than good, and yet they persist relentlessly. The IMF itself has admitted that austerity is much worse for the economy than previously speculated, but that doesn't seem to be stopping them from pursuing it as the primary course of action.

All these measures end up doing is forcing a country to play by the rules predetermined by the hegemonic powers in the international community. They allow control to be established and hinder recovery for the state in need, succeeding in perpetuating the status quo and only aiding in the success of those already in power.
My impression is that they know this isn't the best course of action but they have no clue how else to proceed.

Greece has issued more relaxed reforms to be considered, which would allegedly encourage economic growth, albeit at a much slower pace... Unfortunately, all of these proposals have been turned down almost immediately because they don't meet the incredibly high standards that the IMF endorses.
But what are you supposed to do? If you don't inflict draconian measures the problem will never be solved. If you do, it could make it worse. Where is the middle ground, assuming there is one?
